title: Understanding the Scatter Plot
text: The scatter plot shows a negative correlation between 'mpg' and 'age'. As 'age' increases, 'mpg' decreases. This pattern is important for identifying consistent plots.

title: Analyzing KDE Plots
text: KDE plots (a) and (b) show the distribution of a single variable. Look for a distribution that matches the spread of 'age' or 'mpg' from the scatter plot.

title: Interpreting Histograms
text: Histograms (c) and (d) represent the frequency distribution of a variable. Consider which variable's distribution would appear more uniform or skewed based on the scatter plot.

title: Point Plots Analysis
text: Point plots (e.i), (e.ii), (f.i), and (f.ii) show means and confidence intervals. Determine which variable's mean would be more spread out or clustered based on the scatter plot.

title: Scatter Plots Comparison
text: Scatter plots (g.i), (g.ii), (h.i), and (h.ii) should be compared to the original scatter plot. Look for similar patterns of correlation and clustering.
